Cc: Sara Ling <sara.ling@edgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Slice equity guidelines and temporary rebalance request

Team —

We have an EdgeHealth pilot going live in their staging window tomorrow morning (11/19) that is sprint-critical for their integrated triage demo. They are seeing high tail latency during concurrent synthetic tests; after digging with the SREs we believe the root is slot contention in the us-west dedicated pool (q3-slate).

Ask: Can we temporarily rebalance 12 GPU slots from q3-slate into a short-lived, tagged slice for EdgeHealth for a 48-hour window (start 11/19 06:00 PST) and exempt that allocation from the autoscale preemption policy? This is explicitly to stabilize latency for the demo; we will return capacity on 11/21 06:00 PST.

Why this path:
- Burst lanes are overbooked right now and not giving the predictable tail we need.
- Full reservation procurement would take too long for the demo.
- A short, controlled carve with an autoscale-exception flag (manual override) minimizes customer impact and operational changes.

What I can provide immediately:
- Capacity matrix with current pool assignments (attached: capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx).
- Canary run logs from last night highlighting the 95/99 latency spikes (can attach if ops wants).
- A quick runbook (I can draft) that includes tagging, monitoring dashboards, and an owner for the 48-hour window.

Constraints we should respect: no SLA changes, label the slice with customer and short window, and ensure billing tags are set so Finance can reconcile.

Please respond with: 1) feasibility (yes/no), 2) any prerequisites you need (JIRA, approvals), and 3) who will own the runbook and teardown.

Thanks — I want to avoid routing the customer to a degraded demo.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity

Mina —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attached matrix. Quick thoughts before Ops pulls the lever: 

1) Autoscale exception: we can allow a manual exemption but need an approvals trail (JIRA ticket + approver). Who signs off for finance (billing tag changes)?
2) Allocation: moving 12 slots is feasible in principle but I need to know the exact model families (A100 v2 vs L4s) so we avoid cold-start mismatches. Marcus, can you confirm the compatible model variants?
3) Fallback: If the carve impacts other pilots, we should have a soft-preempt policy — allow preemption for non-critical jobs with a 10-min drain notice. Can David/infra automate that notice?

If you want us to move fast, open an INFRA ticket and @David for the automation piece. I can volunteer Product to own the runbook draft and coordinate tagging/billing with Finance.

Mina / Kim —

Quick technical note: we can reassign 12 slots, but model compatibility is the gating factor. Current q3-slate has a mix: 8 x A100-v2 and 24 x H100-q2 (older label). EdgeHealth is running a 13B LLaMA-variant that prefers the A100-v2 profile. If we allocate pure A100 capacity for the 48h window, we should avoid tokenization or perf mismatches.

Implementation options (fastest -> safest):
1) Manual slice copy: carve 12 A100-v2 slots, tag them edgehealth-sprint, push a manual allocator override. (Time: ~60–90m, low risk if we lock preemption.)
2) Preemptible soft-slice: create a tagged slice and set a preemptible flag on low-priority jobs with a 10-min drain — requires automation rule (30m to enable) and a watch.
3) Canary-first approach: create 4-slot canary with the exact model binary, run validation for 2 hours, and then expand if no regressions. This is slower but reduces rollback risk.

I recommend option 3 given the customer demo impact. I can spin up the canary and run the validation suite if Mina and Laura can own test criteria. Also attaching last-night's canary_run_log.txt excerpt for visibility (I can paste full log to the JIRA).

Approving a controlled, timeboxed allocation for EdgeHealth with the following guardrails:

1) Create INFRA ticket INFRA-4521 (link: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4521) — include capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx and the canary_run_log.txt.
2) Implementation path: do a canary (Marcus option 3). If canary passes validation within 2 hours, expand to the full 12-slot slice.
3) Autoscale exception: grant manual override for the 48-hour window. We will not change the global policy — this is a tagged exception.
4) Teardown: set an automated teardown job for 2026-11-21T06:00:00-08:00 that will untag and return slots to q3-slate. If teardown job fails, ops pager will trigger.
5) Billing: tag the slice with billing:edgehealth-pilot and inform Finance (procurements@novamed.com copied here).

Mina/Marcus: please create the INFRA ticket and attach the runbook (short checklist is fine). I will authorize the exception once INFRA-4521 has the runbook and the canary log attached.
